> The CI failures seems to be upstream issues.

The unit test failure seems to be caused by the new `alibaba` field added in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/7230cd26838a133e93699497d2d27eb59ccf8460#diff-1c36a1df52a01f7e8cd9ef0405d0920b3434be2677cd986b8e19ccdf0d63970aR212-R216 , which is now
fixed in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/321bf1f8e1477dcca1b35173279d145e5fa5bf5a#diff-18cd5a08597420ccf6d67810d813065659815f6b6f7a6578ab9d9907b62d3049R1845-R1907

To give more context on why this matters for plugins: right now if a subagent makes a tool call, the plugin hook only sees the current agent, not who dispatched it. That means any plugin doing delegation policy, same-model-family checks, or audit logging has to build its own tracking layer to figure out the parent-child relationship. The session layer already has this data (parentID in task.ts), this PR just passes it through. Would unblock a lot of plugin governance use cases.

> @simonklee I worked on the same issue in #21177 and ran into a problem with the baseCode approach.
> 
> When I debugged key events with Korean IME on VSCode's integrated terminal and macOS Terminal, baseCode was always undefined: name="ㅊ" ctrl=true baseCode=undefined raw="\x1b[12618;5u" source=kitty
> 
> Most terminals implement Kitty keyboard protocol partially and don't include the baseCode field. So getBaseCodeName() will return undefined, and match() will just compare "c" === "ㅊ" which is false.
> 
> This means the fix won't actually work on VSCode terminal, macOS Terminal, and likely most other terminals that don't send baseCode. That's why I added a character-to-QWERTY mapping table as a fallback in my PR.
> 
> Also, a minor note on the test — "x" is paired with "ㅊ" (baseCode 99), but on Korean 2-Set layout, the x key produces "ㅌ", not "ㅊ". "ㅊ" is the c key.
> 
> Might be worth combining both approaches — use baseCode when available, fall back to a mapping table when it's not.

Thanks — that was actually helpful. We'll keep on iterating on this.

### **Orchestrators don't save you requests, they save you context so your smart orchestrator can keep everything together while your cheaper coders / reviewers don't clog up the orchestrator's context _(particularly important on copilot's miniscule context sizes)._**

Here's Opus explaining how the copilot plugin is instrumented in opencode.

---

## Two-Layer System
The plugin lives at `packages/opencode/src/plugin/copilot.ts` in the OpenCode monorepo.

### Layer 1 — Fetch wrapper (runs on every API call)
Parses the request body to determine `x-initiator`:
- **OpenAI format:** `isAgent = last.role !== "user"` — if the last message is a tool result (role "tool") or assistant, it's agent-initiated
- **Anthropic format:** `isAgent = !(last.role === "user" && hasNonToolCalls)` — special handling for mixed content (tool_result + text in same message)
- **Parse failure:** defaults to `"user"` (conservative — may overcount)

### Layer 2 — `chat.headers` plugin hook (runs before fetch, can override)
Three cases:
1. **Compaction request** → forces `x-initiator: "agent"` (free)
2. **Sub-session (has parentID)** → forces `x-initiator: "agent"` (free)
3. **Neither** → does NOT set header (defers to Layer 1)
**Plugin output spreads AFTER fetch-level**, so the plugin hook wins when it sets a value.

## The Agent → Subagent Chain for 0x orchestrator → 3x subagent.

```
User prompt
  → Orchestrator session (parentID = NULL)
      → Fetch wrapper: last.role = "user" → x-initiator: "user"
      → Plugin hook: no parentID → no override
      → RESULT: BILLED at model multiplier (0× for GPT-4.1)

  → Orchestrator calls Task tool → spawns subagent session (parentID = orchestrator's sessionID)
      → Every API call in subagent:
          → Fetch wrapper: would set "user" or "agent" based on message roles
          → Plugin hook: parentID IS SET → forces "agent" (overrides fetch wrapper)
          → RESULT: FREE — always, regardless of model or message role
```


The parentID check is the mechanism that makes subagent calls unconditionally free. It doesn't matter what model the subagent uses or what the message roles look like — if parentID is set, the plugin forces `"agent"` and billing never sees it.

## Verified: Windows-specific bug in `globalFiles()` path resolution

I've identified the root cause. As you suspected, this is a Windows-only bug.

### The Bug

`Global.Path.config` in `packages/opencode/src/global/index.ts` uses `xdg-basedir`:

```typescript
import { xdgConfig } from "xdg-basedir"
const config = path.join(xdgConfig!, "opencode")
```

On Windows, `xdgConfig` resolves to `%APPDATA%` (`C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming`), **not** `~/.config/`.

So `globalFiles()` in `packages/opencode/src/session/instruction.ts` (line 30) looks for:

```
C:\Users\Sanve\AppData\Roaming\opencode\AGENTS.md  ← DOES NOT EXIST
```

But my actual AGENTS.md is at:

```
C:\Users\Sanve\.config\opencode\AGENTS.md  ← EXISTS
```

### Non-LLM Verification

1. **Read the source code** — `globalFiles()` at line 30 does `path.join(Global.Path.config, "AGENTS.md")`, and `Global.Path.config = path.join(xdgConfig!, "opencode")` from `global/index.ts` line 6.

2. **Checked xdg-basedir resolution on Windows**:
   ```
   APPDATA=C:\Users\Sanve\AppData\Roaming
   → xdgConfig = C:\Users\Sanve\AppData\Roaming
   → Global.Path.config = C:\Users\Sanve\AppData\Roaming\opencode
   ```

3. **Confirmed filesystem mismatch**:
   - `C:\Users\Sanve\AppData\Roaming\opencode\` exists but contains only runtime data (EBWebView, quotas-debug.log) — no AGENTS.md
   - `C:\Users\Sanve\.config\opencode\AGENTS.md` exists with my rules

4. **Confirmed in OpenCode logs** — Config loading correctly reads from `.config\opencode\` (logs show `service=config path=C:\Users\Sanve\.config\opencode\opencode.json loading`), meaning the config path resolution has special handling for `opencode.json` but NOT for AGENTS.md via `globalFiles()`.

### Why it works on Unix

On Linux/macOS, `xdgConfig` resolves to `~/.config/`, which matches where users naturally place their config. On Windows, `xdgConfig` resolves to `%APPDATA%` instead, creating a mismatch with the `~/.config/opencode/` directory that OpenCode itself creates and uses for other config files.

### The Fix

`globalFiles()` should search additional paths on Windows, or `Global.Path.config` should be consistent with where OpenCode actually stores its config. Since OpenCode already reads `opencode.json` from `~/.config/opencode/` on Windows, the AGENTS.md loading should check the same directory.
